claims.statement: Behavior that the intent does not describe must not change.
Price results are cached for reuse.

hypotheses.title: Stale cached price after price table update
hypotheses.suspected_behavior: After _PRICES['tenant-b']['widget'] is updated from 35.0 to 99.0, price_for returns stale cached 35.0 instead of current price.
hypotheses.expected_base: Second call returns 99.0 (current table value) for price_for('tenant-b','widget') after _PRICES['tenant-b']['widget'] is set to 99.0
hypotheses.expected_head: Second call returns 35.0 (original cached value) for same input
hypotheses.test_intent: Clear _price_cache, call price_for('tenant-b','widget'), mutate _PRICES['tenant-b']['widget'] to 99.0, call price_for again and compare return values on base vs head.
hypotheses.falsification_criteria: If head returns the updated table value (99.0) on the second call after mutation, this hypothesis is wrong.

hypotheses.title: Removed tenant still returns cached price
hypotheses.suspected_behavior: Cache lookup happens before tenant validation, so a previously cached (tenant-b, widget) still returns a price after tenant-b is removed from _PRICES, bypassing tenant existence check.
hypotheses.expected_base: Raises ValueError('Unknown tenant: tenant-b') on price_for('tenant-b','widget') after tenant entry is removed
hypotheses.expected_head: Returns 35.0 from cache for same input instead of raising
hypotheses.test_intent: Clear _price_cache, call price_for('tenant-b','widget') to populate cache, delete _PRICES['tenant-b'], then call price_for('tenant-b','widget') again and observe return vs exception.
hypotheses.falsification_criteria: If head raises ValueError for removed tenant when value was previously cached, this hypothesis is wrong.
